We also discovered that the model's residual patterns are consistent across all days of the year, with some exceptions during holidays and weekends. We introduce a new family of degenerate Stirling numbers, denoted as $\tilde{r}_{k}(n)$, with a direct relationship to the classic Stirling numbers of the second kind. These numbers count how many ways a set with $n$ elements can be divided into a specific number of non-empty subsets, each containing $k$ elements, where the number $r$ determines the allowed partition configurations. formalized guarantees in their standard implementations.

algorithm, which provides a framework for ensuring fairness and price 
stability in auctions that involve multiple buyers and sellers.
The paper also includes a case study of its application to program trading 
systems, demonstrating how the model can be used to guarantee fair prices

verification tools are available online.

Over-smoothing significantly limits the potential of Graph Convolutional Networks, causing them to fail in complex graph classification tasks. The over-smoothing phenomenon is characterized by the excessive reduction of node features, which can be attributed to the Graph Convolutional Networks' reliance on local averaging methods. Our findings reveal that Graph Convolutional Networks are only effective in addressing classification tasks involving well-structured graphs with clear hierarchies. Conversely, they are unsuitable for tasks involving complex, disordered graphs. Furthermore, we propose a novel approach to mitigate the over-smoothing effect, which involves the incorporation of skip connections within Graph Convolutional Networks. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of this approach in enhancing node feature retention and graph classification accuracy. user-generated content. By employing a network analysis approach, we examine
the temporal evolution of these systems and uncover the underlying factors
that contribute to their development. Our findings reveal that the initial

gradually gives way to increased reuse of existing tags. This is further
supported by the presence of a core group of users who drive the system's
evolution. Additionally, our analysis suggests that the interest of users
converges over time, leading to a more cohesive system. Notably, our study
also identifies a subset of users who exhibit exceptional collaboration
capabilities. Our research provides a comprehensive understanding of the
complex dynamics at play within collaborative tagging systems. By mapping
these patterns, we can inform the development of more effective systems

framework for the analysis of other user-generated content platforms. By

mechanisms that govern these systems and their evolution over time. Our
research can serve as a foundation for the development of more sophisticated
models that capture the intricate nature of collaborative tagging systems.

A novel enhancement to RingCT, a widely used transaction privacy protocol, is presented in this paper. The improvement, known as Delegated RingCT, accelerates transaction processing on the DECO cryptocurrency by leveraging a consensus mechanism to pre-select a group of stealth addresses. This optimization enables Delegated RingCT transactions to bypass the need for complex public key and signature verification, resulting in significantly faster transaction validation times. Experimental results demonstrate that Delegated RingCT transactions are approximately 2-3 times faster to validate than traditional RingCT transactions. Furthermore, the study examines the impact of varying factors on transaction processing speed, including the number of participating nodes and the level of user anonymity. The research also explores the potential security risks associated with delegating the stealth address selection process. The findings indicate that Delegated RingCT offers a suitable solution for supporting high-performance transaction processing within decentralized systems. The paper concludes by outlining future research directions for enhancing the scalability of RingCT-based protocols. Recent studies have demonstrated the potential of large language models to
perform in-context learning, but the impact of training data on this capability
remains unclear. This research investigates the influence of various datasets on
in-context learning by examining the performance of a 137B-parameter model on
five diverse tasks. Our analysis reveals that models trained on specialized
datasets excel in corresponding in-context learning tasks, but when confronted
with tasks outside their training scope, they often underperform compared to
models trained on more comprehensive datasets. Furthermore, we identify a
notable correlation between training data size and in-context learning
effectiveness. Our findings suggest that models can develop a 'domain
expertise,' which may be beneficial but also limits their adaptability. To
facilitate future research, we have made our data and code available at

We introduce a novel approach called the Cauchy--Taylor--Krylov method (CTTK) 
for resolving the equations governing initial conditions in numerical relativity.
This method, derived from the Taylor--Krylov method, efficiently iterates the 
initial data equations by leveraging the spectral properties of the associated 
matrices. Consequently, CTTK exhibits a direct correlation with the 
condition number of these matrices, thereby enabling the estimation of 
required iterations for any given precision level. Furthermore, our method 
is characterized by minimal memory usage and linear computational complexity, 
making it particularly suitable for applications in numerical relativity. 
Through a series of tests, we demonstrate the efficacy of CTTK in resolving 
initial conditions for a range of scenarios, including black hole and neutron 
star simulations. Notably, our method outperforms existing techniques in terms 
of convergence speed and stability. Additionally, we provide a publicly 
accessible implementation of CTTK in the form of a Python package. 
This package can be accessed via the following repository: 
https://github.com/numerical-relativity/cttk. 
We envision that CTTK will serve as a versatile tool for a broad range of 
applications in numerical relativity.

size. This approach enables efficient asynchronous aggregation without requiring 
bounded gradients. We provide a theoretical framework for its convergence and 
demonstrate its effectiveness through experiments. Additionally, we explore the 
connection between buffered aggregation and traditional averaging methods. Our 
findings show that buffered aggregation can be seen as a form of averaging with 
weighted noise, which has significant implications for its performance and 
stability. Furthermore, we highlight the potential risks of buffered 
aggregation and discuss strategies for mitigating these issues. Our code is 
available at https://github.com/alexandre-matton/bufagg.

The process of magnetic reconnection is a significant phenomenon that can lead to the release of a substantial amount of magnetic energy. In the context of the solar corona, this process is often linked to the occurrence of solar flares. A numerical investigation of magnetic reconnection is presented, focusing on the coalescence of magnetic islands within a toroidal, twisted flux rope. The simulation employed the MP5 MHD model in combination with the AEMPIC model, allowing for the adaptation of spatial resolution based on local current density. The results showed that the magnetic islands coalesced into a single, central island, accompanied by the formation of a current sheet. The associated energy dissipation was found to be consistent with Sweet-Parker theory. Additionally, the current sheet's thickness was observed to be directly proportional to the island's width. The findings of this study support the potential application of the adapted AEMPIC model in simulating complex magnetic reconnection processes. Furthermore, the results suggest that the model can accurately capture the dynamics of magnetic reconnection without relying on a predetermined current sheet thickness. The study's outcomes are expected to contribute to a deeper understanding of the phenomenon of magnetic reconnection.
